topics.title: Dying on Toad's Place
topics.summary: A couple’s sailing trip turns disastrous when they forget flares and resort to drinking urine while rationing dwindling supplies, leading to an engagement toast fueled by desperation. The situation escalates with the man’s decision not to purchase essential equipment like a water purifier or radio transmitter, further complicated by their strained interactions and eventual shared survival strategy.

topics.title: Frank Sinatra Weekend Offer & Jessica Hahn
topics.summary: Howard promotes a $25,000 weekend experience with Frank Sinatra in Rancho Mirage and Las Vegas including private plane travel, cocktails, dinner shows, and a roast hosted by Tommy Lasorda. A secondary offering is a pay-per-view event featuring Jessica Hahn as the host of 'Thunder & Mud' alongside metal bands.

topics.title: Woodstock Minute - Drunken Revelations
topics.summary: A chaotic radio interview reveals a drunken Larry Fine recounting his experiences at Woodstock, including bizarre interactions with Country Joe and the Fish, drug use, accusations of exploitation by Warner Brothers, and increasingly nonsensical statements about lighting guitars on fire.

topics.title: Confused Casting & Woodstock Memories
topics.summary: During an interview, host Howard discusses casting calls for Mr. Magoo and challenges of finding suitable voices while recounting his attempt to audition himself. He also shares a bizarre anecdote about attempting to induce dizziness during the infamous Woodstock performance with amyl nitrates.

topics.title: Woodstock Minute - Mattress & Magoo
topics.summary: During the broadcast, hosts Allison Steele and an unidentified host discuss obtaining Woodstock tickets while engaging in nonsensical conversations about mattresses, dial-a-mattress services, and referencing Jim Backus (Magoo). They make random calls and attempt to understand weather patterns.

topics.title: Atlanta Radio Broadcast Promotes Racial Fears
topics.summary: A radio broadcast in Atlanta discusses escalating racial tensions fueled by perceived homosexual influence and political power within the city. The speaker promotes racist stereotypes about Vietnamese, Mexican, and Black people while advocating for discriminatory policies and a violent removal of minority groups from Gainesville, Georgia.
